A.explanation: Area under velocity-time is $velocity \times time$, which gives displacement, so it does give a required value.

B.explanation: Gradient of displacement-time is $\Delta s / \Delta t$, which gives velocity, so it does give a required value.

C.explanation: Gradient of velocity-time is $\Delta v / \Delta t$, which gives acceleration, so it does give a required value.

D.explanation: Gradient of acceleration-time is $\Delta a / \Delta t$, the rate of change of acceleration, not a displacement, velocity or acceleration.

hints: Look at what gradient means for each graph: $\Delta y / \Delta x$ using the axis labels displacement $s$, velocity $v$, acceleration $a$ and time $t$.
Recall that velocity is rate of change of displacement and acceleration is rate of change of velocity, so check which gradients match those definitions.
Check the units: $\Delta a / \Delta t$ has units $\text{m s}^{-3}$, which is not $\text{m}$, $\text{m s}^{-1}$ or $\text{m s}^{-2}$, while area under acceleration-time would give velocity.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: gradient of a motion graph gives $y$-quantity divided by $x$-quantity, and area under the graph gives $y$-quantity multiplied by $x$-quantity.
Apply to area under velocity-time: $v \times t$ has units $\text{m s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{m}$, so it gives displacement.
Apply to gradient of displacement-time: $\Delta s / \Delta t$ gives velocity, and gradient of velocity-time: $\Delta v / \Delta t$ gives acceleration.
Apply to gradient of acceleration-time: $\Delta a / \Delta t$ gives rate of change of acceleration with unit $\text{m s}^{-3}$, which is not displacement, velocity or acceleration. This is option D.
